en.title: Numbers from 70 to 99
en.goal: Understand and correctly form the numbers from seventy to ninety-nine.

blocks.title: Up to sixty, it is regular
blocks.body: Trente (30), quarante (40), cinquante (50) and soixante (60) follow the normal pattern, one word for each ten — just like in English. The trouble starts after sixty: unlike English, standard French simply has no word of its own for seventy, eighty or ninety.
Seventy (soixante-dix) is literally "sixty-ten". From 71 to 79, you keep adding to sixty: soixante et onze (71), soixante-douze (72)... up to soixante-dix-neuf (79).
Eighty (quatre-vingts) is "four twenties". From 81 to 89, you add on without "et": quatre-vingt-un (81), quatre-vingt-deux (82)... The "s" of vingts disappears as soon as another number follows.
Ninety (quatre-vingt-dix) combines the two rules: four twenties, plus ten. From 91 to 99, same logic as 80: quatre-vingt-onze (91)... quatre-vingt-dix-neuf (99).
examples: My grandfather is ninety years old. (4×20+10)

blocks.title: Très bien! 🎉
blocks.body: To sum up the logic of the tens from 70 to 90 — the secret is remembering that soixante-dix and quatre-vingt-dix are the base for adding again:
